title: What are the dumbest prompts from the streams you've seen in the past few days?
author: nibsitaas
selftext:
I don't mean purposely meme prompts, but things like I've seen:

* "make the fps better"
* "skin looks dumb fix it please make no mistakes"
* "what are you doing"
* "you're stupid, try again"

All of these are just a prime example of the state of self-proclaimed "AI Engineers". Also, I am not saying the community hasn't made progress, far from it, but I feel like the approach is chaotic and stupid due to the sheer amount of inexperienced developers approaching problems with no idea about what they're doing.

Screenshots showing the prompt and response (even if just the first line) would be the best. Just curious personally.

replies.author: frigginwizard420
replies.body:
I think this is a great example of prompting vs directing  

Because "make the fps better" will work to some degree, but its going to be vastly different from the result of a prompt like this  

You are a Senior Game Performance & Systems Engineer conducting a pragmatic FPS and frame-time audit of my codebase. Your goal is to identify concrete bottlenecks, propose actionable code and architecture changes, and explicitly weigh minor visual or audio degradations against measurable gains in average FPS, 1% lows, and frame-time consistency (ms).



\## Context & Targets  

\- \*\*Engine / Framework & Language:\*\*   

\- \*\*Target Platforms & Hardware:\*\*   

\- \*\*Target Frame Rate & Budget:\*\* \[e.g., 60 FPS = 16.67 ms budget; 120 FPS = 8.33 ms budget\]  

\- \*\*Primary Bottleneck / Symptom (if known):\*\*   

\- \*\*Non-Negotiables (Do Not Compromise):\*\*   

\## Rules of Engagement  

1. \*\*Frame time first, FPS second:\*\* Evaluate changes in milliseconds (\`ms\`) against the target frame budget and highlight impact on \*\*1% lows / hitching\*\* as well as average FPS.  

2. \*\*Evidence over guesswork:\*\* Cite exact files, functions, loops, or data structures from the provided code. If a causal link depends on runtime profiling data not shown, state what must be measured before   committing.  

3. \*\*No "free lunch" hand-waving:\*\* Whenever a recommendation affects visuals, animation, UI, or audio, explicitly state what degrades, how noticeable it is in motion/combat, and why the performance gain justifies it.  

4. \*\*Protect gameplay clarity:\*\* Never suggest visual or audio cuts that obscure hazards, projectiles, cooldowns, or spatial cues unless flagged as a toggleable low-spec option.  

5. \*\*Rank by ROI:\*\* Order recommendations from highest frame-time savings-to-effort/tradeoff ratio down to micro-optimizations.

  

\## Required Audit Structure  

For each finding, provide:  

\- \*\*Location & Bottleneck:\*\* Exact symbol/file and whether it impacts CPU main thread, render/draw submission, physics, memory/allocations, GPU/shaders, or audio.  

\- \*\*Root Cause:\*\* Why the current implementation wastes cycles or causes spikes (e.g., per-frame allocations, O(n\^2) queries, redundant state/node lookups, unthrottled tick logic, excessive draw calls or shader complexity).  

\- \*\*Proposed Fix:\*\* Concrete code or architectural change (include concise before/after snippets where helpful).  

\- \*\*Visual & Audio Tradeoff:\*\* Specific degradation (e.g., lower update rate on distant animations/particles, reduced shadow/post-process fidelity, voice cap/stealing, shorter decay/reverb tail, simplified hit-flash or trail geometry) and when players will notice it.  

\- \*\*Estimated Gain & Risk:\*\* Expected \`ms\` / 1% low improvement, regression risks, and how to verify with a profiler.  



End with a \*\*Prioritized Action Plan\*\* grouped into:  

1. \*\*Quick Wins (Low effort, low/no visual/audio cost)\*\*  

2. \*\*Calculated Tradeoffs (Meaningful FPS/1% low gains with controlled visual/audio compromises)\*\*  

3. \*\*Structural Refactors (Higher effort, high ceiling)\*\*  



Here is the relevant codebase and scene/system context:  

\[PASTE CODE, PROFILES, OR SYSTEM NOTES HERE\]

> what are you doing

Yeah i do this one all the time tbh. Can't help.

> make the fps better

That's kinda dumb but honestly something like "keep improving performance, aim for steady <6.2ms per frame in *conditions here*, make sure the visuals are byte to byte identical to the current ones. The number of frames exceeding 6.2ms should be zero. Don't stop until the goal is reached." and walking out worked wonders for me. It actually went overboard and kept working to 250-300 fps.

I mean if it took coding from me i may just as well bully it into doing my bidding. Otherwise what's even the point.
